question: Does a MinGW-w64 C++11 static library, linked into a MinGW-w64 Win32 executable, run on Windows 2000 SP4?
result: DECISION (project owner, 2026-11-13): S1 is confirmed on the strength of the Windows 2000 build 2195 (no service pack) trial below. The owner accepts that what runs without a service pack also runs with SP4, because service packs only add or fix exports and keep the ones the executable imports (all 112 imports exist in the RTM DLLs). This is an inference, NOT a measurement: SP4 itself, and its newer msvcrt.dll, were never run. Open, kept open on purpose: the question names Windows 2000 SP4 and the system tested has NO service pack (RTM, build 2195), so SP4 is still untested, and T066 asks for a Windows 2000 SP4 VM, which this VM is not; everything else the question asks (a static C++11 library linked into a Win32 executable, plus the backend self-test) ran on the RTM system; the lead decides the status. TRIAL (2026-11-12): Windows 2000 Professional build 2195, no service pack, English (US), in a VirtualBox 7.2.22 VM (1 vCPU, 168 MB RAM, Guest Additions 6.1.18) on the Windows 11 host; records validation/platforms/windows-2000-x86.json and validation/verdicts/windows-2000-x86-legacy.json (ok_restricted), evidence in validation/evidence/first-trial/windows-2000-x86/, tooling in adr/0003-win2000-vm-unicode-launcher.md. WHAT RAN AND WORKED: the backend self-test (see BACKEND SELF-TEST below) and the i686 Legacy UI executable (694,005 bytes: the MinGW-w64 GCC 13 C++11 static library libloomora.a linked into a Win32 exe with libstdc++ and libgcc static, ADR 0002 shim for GetThreadId) loads and runs. All 112 imports of the executable are exported by the real kernel32.dll 5.0.2191.1, user32.dll 5.0.2180.1, gdi32.dll 5.0.2180.1 and msvcrt.dll 6.1.8637.0 of that system (export tables read; 0 missing), and all 117 functions of the x86 allowlist tools/win2000_imports.json are exported (0 missing); the 12 entries marked verify (TryEnterCriticalSection, the msvcrt.dll start-up internals) are now verified-on-vm for x86 (RTM export tables, not SP4's). The window shows the end-of-life banner, 'Bonjour Coucou', and 'Bonjour Marie' when typed with the virtual keyboard (screenshots); 20 of 20 probe runs: exit 0, display_ms 3 to 13, peak_rss_kb 1084 (checked plausible with memtest and WMI, not a defect), no process left; 15 of 15 reference vectors and 25 of 25 extra hard texts (emoji, CJK, right-to-left, controls, quotes, backslashes, %PATH%, 1,500 characters) round-trip unchanged; exits by itself after 2 s and with Alt+F4. Skipped features on this system: dpi-awareness (user32 does not export SetProcessDPIAware) and dark-mode (no AppsUseLightTheme); GetNativeSystemInfo is absent and the fallback GetSystemInfo is taken; dwmapi.dll is absent. BACKEND SELF-TEST (first attempt failed, fixed, now passes): loomora_selftest cross-built with cmake/toolchains/mingw-w64-win2000-i686.cmake did NOT load on Windows 2000 at first: it imported KERNEL32!GetThreadId (removed by the ADR 0002 shim) and, with or without the shim, four Vista-only functions (InitializeConditionVariable, SleepConditionVariableCS, WakeConditionVariable, WakeAllConditionVariable) from libgcc.a(gthr-win32-cond.o), pulled in by its use of <iostream> (libstdc++ ios_init); the loader refused it (exit status 128, no output), exactly like a control program importing InitializeConditionVariable (selftest-output.txt, the first attempt). The Legacy UI, which links the same libloomora.a but no iostream, was never affected. DECISION taken: keep <iostream> out of core/tests/selftest.cpp (output through std::fputs; std::printf is avoided too because MinGW-w64 maps it to __mingw_vfprintf, which imports msvcrt _lock and _unlock, not on the allowlist) and link the GetThreadId shim into the 32-bit selftest (core/tests/CMakeLists.txt compiles the shim source of the UI; no code duplicated); no extension of the shim, no other toolchain (research R6 fallback 2) was needed. RESULT (2026-11-13): the rebuilt loomora_selftest.exe (sha256 638449ff8e1aeb77a2905d5f5403b2843dc9f766c2f5a138b3bc0574403cdb89, 629,857 bytes) has 67 imports from kernel32 and msvcrt, 0 outside the Windows 2000 SP4 allowlist and 0 not exported by the real DLLs of the VM (117 of 117 allowlist functions exported again); started from a .bat in the guest it printed 'all passed' and ended with exit code 0 (selftest-noiostream-vm-run.txt and .json, selftest-noiostream-imports.txt, selftest-noiostream-vm-exports.txt in validation/evidence/selftest-no-iostream/windows-2000-x86/); the control without the shim still imports GetThreadId and the loader refuses it (errorlevel 128), so the shim stays necessary. The same sources pass on Windows 11 (i686 under WOW64 and x86_64, MinGW-w64), with the host build and ctest, and on Linux (ctest, tools/check_std.py): selftest-noiostream-regression.txt. The selftest covers only the greet vectors, loomora_abi_version and loomora_build_compiler. STILL UNVERIFIED: Windows 2000 SP4 (and the SP4 msvcrt.dll, which is a later build than this RTM one); real hardware instead of VirtualBox; other languages, editions and machines; a person typing, IME, clipboard, a high contrast scheme, DPI above 96; the behaviour of a C++ exception thrown in the static runtime (none was thrown); the 1,000-character EDIT limit by keyboard on this system; Windows 2000 x64 does not exist (N/A); XP and later (S9) and the x64 executable on XP x64 / Server 2003 x64 are not covered.

question: Does modern Clang + osxcross + the 10.6 SDK run on 10.6; does Xcode 5.1.1 build and deploy to iOS 5?

With which toolchain can the backend, the JNI glue and the APK be built for API 9 on armeabi, armeabi-v7a, x86 and arm64-v8a, and how many of those builds can be run on the emulators available (none below API 16)? HISTORY: the first wording of this spike was "does NDK r16b + the scripted APK build run on an Android 2.3 emulator (all four ABIs)?"; it was refuted on 2026-11-14 (NDK r16b has no android-9 platform; r15c has it but its ndk-build raises APP_PLATFORM below 14 to 14) and the question was rewritten to the one above.
result: Confirmed on 2026-11-15 for the rewritten question. HISTORY: status `refuted` on 2026-11-14 for the first wording (NDK r16b + ndk-build); the owner asked to rewrite the question and record `confirmed`, keeping the trace. a CMake toolchain file that drives NDK r15c Clang directly with the android-9 sysroot (android-21 for arm64-v8a) builds libloomora_jni.so and loomora_selftest for armeabi, armeabi-v7a, x86 and arm64-v8a (gnustl static, DT_NEEDED libc.so, plus libdl.so on x86 and arm64-v8a, link with --no-undefined against the API 9 libraries, armeabi needs -latomic); build-tools 36 d8 --min-api 9 and javac -source 8 + aapt + zipalign + apksigner v1 give one APK of the four ABIs (228,623 bytes on 2026-11-14, 228,663 bytes since the package rename to fr.bansan.loomora, same libraries). RUN: only x86, on an Android 4.1.2 (API 16) emulator, the oldest that can be started: loomora_selftest 'all passed', the APK installs and shows the greeting, 15 of 15 reference vectors pass (rerun on the renamed APK on 2026-11-15, API 16 and API 24, see the verdicts). NOT DONE, and not possible with the emulators of this project: running on Android 2.3 to 4.0 (API 9 to 15) and any ARM ABI (no ARM system image or device). The claim 'runs on Android 2.3' is neither confirmed nor refuted, T068 stays unticked and T091 stays partial.
fallback: NDK r15c + CMake toolchain file + scripted APK build instead of NDK r16b + ndk-build (ADR 0016)

question: Does the JavaScript build run on IE 9 / Firefox 8 / Chrome 15 / Safari 5.1 / Opera 11.5; modern Emscripten or fastcomp 1.39.20?
Does the backend compile with strict C++11 under GCC and Clang and export only C symbols, with every exception caught at the C boundary?
result: Confirmed on Linux (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, libstdc++): tools/check_std.py passes with g++ 13.3.0 and clang++ 23.1.5. Checked for each: all 6 core/src/*.cpp compile with -std=c++11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror; loomora.h compiles as C89 (-std=c89 -pedantic-errors, gcc 13.3.0 / clang 23.1.5) and as C++98; a shared library built with -fvisibility=hidden exports exactly the 6 loomora_* C functions (nm -D --defined-only), with the C++ runtime linked dynamically and statically (-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc); core/tests/boundary_check.cpp makes every allocation of every loomora_* call fail in turn (28 failures injected with GCC, 30 with Clang) and no exception escapes. Finding: -fvisibility=hidden alone is NOT enough, libstdc++ marks namespace std as default visibility and std template instantiations leaked into the exports (4 with g++, 16 with clang++); fixed with a link-time export list (core/loomora.map, core/loomora.exp for macOS) that CMake and check_std.py apply to the shared library. Not checked: strict C++11 with clang on Windows (clang 23.1.1 uses the MSVC STL, which needs C++14: the checker reports it as skipped; only the C89/C++98 header checks ran there), libc++, MSVC, Windows DLL exports (__declspec macros untested), macOS exports (loomora.exp untested), and the old compilers of the oldest platforms (S1-S4).

question: Can the 10.6 SDK and Xcode 5.1.1 be obtained legitimately?

Can WinUI 3 call a C++11 loomora.dll, and what is the lowest minSdk at which Jetpack Compose with the pinned AndroidX versions builds? HISTORY: the first wording asked "does Compose accept minSdk 21?"; the answer is no (the pinned libraries declare minSdk 23), so that wording is refuted as stated; the question was rewritten to the one above at the owner's request.
result: Confirmed on 2026-11-15 for the rewritten question. HISTORY: recorded `refuted` on 2026-11-15 for the first wording (Compose accepts minSdk 21), then rewritten and recorded `confirmed` at the owner's request, keeping this trace. WinUI half, CONFIRMED: WinUI 3 (C#, Windows App SDK 2.6.5, unpackaged and framework-dependent, .NET SDK 10.0.404) calls the C++11 loomora.dll through LibraryImport (no C++/CLI, no C++/WinRT) on Windows 11 x64: loomora.dll is built by MSVC 14.52.37025 (cl.exe 19.52.37029, /MT, cl.exe's default /std:c++14 since MSVC has no /std:c++11, the sources stay C++11), exports exactly the six loomora_* functions and imports KERNEL32.dll only (x64 and ARM64 built; ARM64 not run). The ABI check, the greeting, the end-of-life test and the probe record all come from the DLL; 15 of 15 reference vectors pass through the WinUI window in probe mode, for the net10.0 build and for the net8.0 build (Windows App SDK 2.6.5 accepts net8.0, no older SDK needed); the net8 build starts on a machine that has only .NET 10 or only .NET 11 with RollForward Major. Published folder 37.8 MB (zip 9.9 MB) with only the WinUI and Runtime components of the SDK (81.9 MB with the Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK metapackage). Not run: Windows 10 1809, ARM64 execution. Evidence validation/evidence/winui3/windows-11-x64/, verdict validation/verdicts/windows-11-x64-modern.json, procedure validation/procedures/windows.md part C. Android half, REFUTED: Compose with the pinned AndroidX versions (AGP 9.5.1, Gradle 9.9.1, Kotlin 2.3.21, Compose BOM 2026.09.00, activity-compose 1.13.0) does NOT accept minSdk 21: `python tools/build.py android modern --min-sdk 21` fails in the manifest merger, androidx.compose.animation:animation-core-android:1.12.1 declares minSdk 23 (evidence validation/evidence/android-modern/android-7.0-x86_64/spike-s8-minsdk21.txt). tools:overrideLibrary would hide the check but may fail at run time and was not tried. The decided floor 24 stays: minSdk 24 builds and runs on an API 24 x86_64 emulator (15 of 15 vectors, validation/verdicts/android-7.0-x86_64-modern.json).
fallback: Compose minSdk 24 instead of 21 (decided floor; the Android Legacy UI covers API 9 to 23); WinUI half needs none
